subject: adding moderator to multiple paths in a mediation

messages.author: 8319c8b99e0f55e2
messages.subject: adding moderator to multiple paths in a mediation
parts:
Dear experts and community,

I am currently wanting to add a moderator to my mediation model. However, I have been told to add the moderator to all paths of the model (a, b, and c') to figure out at which point the moderator has an effect on the model. This seems to be possible in other packages such as PROCESS, but with Lavaan, it results in the 'duplicate model element' error, which makes sense as I am duplicating the effect of the moderator on both the b and c' paths (which have the same outcome, Y).

Is there a way to get around this in Lavaan, or should I test three separate models (with the moderator being on the a, b, and c' paths separately)? Alternatively, I can also specify models with the moderator on just the a and b paths, or a and c paths, but not sure if I can justify this, without having it also on the third path.

My syntax is as follows:
        # a path
         mediator ~ 1 + a1 * X
         mediator ~ a2 * moderator
         mediator ~ a3 * interaction (between X and moderator)

         # b paths
         Y ~ 1 + b1 * mediator
         Y ~ b2 * moderator
         Y ~ b3 * interaction (between mediator and moderator)
        
         # c prime path 
         Y ~ 1 + cp * X
         Y ~ c2 * moderator
         Y ~ c3 * interaction (between X and moderator)

The highlighted text shows the duplicate - could I run the model after deleting one of the duplicates?

I apologise if these are naive questions as I do not have a strong statistical background - any help would be greatly appreciated!

If you look at the statistical graph of PROCESS model 59, you will see that w (the moderator) is modeled only once as a direct effect on y. Everything else makes little sense.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: adding moderator to multiple paths in a mediation
parts: it results in the 'duplicate model element' error, which makes sense as I am duplicating the effect of the moderator on both the b and c' paths (which have the same outcome, Y).

You are using a single variable "interaction" to represent 2 different product terms? (X*W and M*W)

See the statistical representation of Model 59 for clues:


 
It might help you to actually create the product terms in your data.frame and name them XW and MW to match the path diagram.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: adding moderator to multiple paths in a mediation
parts:
Thank you for your replies - I think I'm now heading towards the right direction, and have edited my syntax according to Model 59:

         # a path
         M ~ 1 + a1 * X 
         M ~ a2 * W
         M ~ a3 * XW
         
         # b path
         Y ~ 1 + b1 * M
         Y ~ b2 * MW
         
         # c prime path 
         Y ~ c1 * X
         Y ~ c2 * W
         Y ~ c3 * XW

There is one more part I am not sure about, which is trying to get the indices of the indirect and direct effects. My moderator is binary (1 or 2) so I've specified the code as below: 

         # index of moderated mediation and conditional indirect effects of XW on a path
         b1a3 := b1 * a3
         aELS1ss := a1 + a3 * 1 # simple slope for when moderator is 1
         aELS2ss := a1 + a3 * 2 # simple slope for when moderator is 2
         aELS1 := a1 * b1 + b1a3 * 1 # indirect effect
         aELS2 := a1 * b1 + b1a3 * 2
         
         # index of moderated mediation and conditional indirect effects of MW on b path
         a1b2 := a1 * b2
         bELS1ss := b1 + b2 * 1 
         bELS2ss := b1 + b2 * 2
         bELS1 := a1 * b1 + a1b2 * 1 # indirect effect
         bELS2 := a1 * b1 + a1b2 * 2
         
         # index of moderated mediation and direct effects of XW on c path
         c1c3 := c1 * c3
         cELS1ss := c1 + c3 * 1
         cELS2ss := c1 + c3 * 2
         cELS1 := c1 + c1c3 * 1 # direct effect
         cELS2 := c1 + c1c3 * 2

It would be immensely helpful if anyone could let me know whether this is the correct way of specifying the effects. The syntax runs as is, so I'm not sure if I've specified everything as I should.

Thank you so much in advance.
